# Care with a Compass — The Director’s Desk · v10.7.4

**Live review:** https://rstenlund1.github.io/care-with-a-compass/?v=10.7.4

**Scenario-placement correction:** The parent inspection/recording scenario now appears in Chapter 3 (Licensing, Ratios & Daily Operations), rather than Chapter 6 (Fairness, Bias & Belonging). The unauthorized pickup scenario now belongs to Chapter 4; the fairness chapter has a new relevant case about selective surveillance of a Black child. The multiple-perspective exercises are explicitly mapped to their matching chapters, and the former Chapter 5 extra-lens rendering path was removed. Includes v10.7.3 single-navigation and concise progress-notice corrections. This is a source-level correction; independent live-browser and expert validation are still required.

# Care with a Compass — The Director’s Desk · v10.7.0

**Live preview:** https://rstenlund1.github.io/care-with-a-compass/?v=10.7.0

**New in v10.7.0:** A sixth foundational chapter, **Fairness, Bias & Belonging**, examines racialized behavior labels, socioeconomic judgments, family language access, disability-related exclusion, consistent child-safety decisions, and disproportionality in incident reports. It includes 12 original questions, eight conditional question follow-ups, and a four-path, two-stage leadership scenario. Sources include the U.S. Department of Education Civil Rights Data Collection, Yale Child Study Center, Head Start 45 CFR §1302.17, California CDSS exclusion guidance, and DOJ disability-access guidance. The foundation now contains **six chapters, 84 applied questions, and 44 follow-ups**; earlier five-chapter progress is preserved, but Chapter 6 is required for current completion.

**One unified operations page:** The director's desired salary and separate business-profit goal appear first. Staffing decisions, coverage consequences, labor costs, county/area/actual rent overrides, overnight and respite revenue, expenses, break-even enrollment, and required tuition then appear in one scrollable page with no separate staffing-versus-budget tabs. Selected extra backup coverage can affect the monthly financial model without counting it twice if the director confirms it is already in regular payroll.

**Validation boundary:** Source data and JavaScript syntax have been checked, but no cohort, clinical or regulatory expert validation, screen-reader audit, full graphical browser regression, live forms check, or measured financial outcomes are claimed. Benchmarks are dated regional retail rent proxies, and the statewide fallback is an illustrative unweighted average, not a true child care lease survey. Verify current laws, rates, staffing, and learner outcomes before use.

**Adversarial review:** [docs/GEMINI_REVIEW_v10.7.0.txt](docs/GEMINI_REVIEW_v10.7.0.txt)

# Care with a Compass — The Director’s Desk · v10.6.0

**Live program:** https://rstenlund1.github.io/care-with-a-compass/?v=10.6.0

**New in v10.6.0:** A persistent overall training progress bar and integrated Staffing & Tuition Planner. The existing staffing-safety exercise remains intact. The financial tool separately models paid teachers, aides, desired director salary, and a business profit target; full-time, part-time, overnight-only and respite income; staffing taxes and benefits, rent, utilities, insurance, food and incidentals; target tuition and estimated break-even enrollment. Learners can use examples or retain their real scenario independently, select any California county, use square-footage rent estimates and a source-dated eight-region retail rent proxy, or override with their actual rent. **Financial data are examples, not audited facility averages or guaranteed tuition recommendations.** The statewide fallback is an unweighted regional planning estimate, not a published state series. The page reads the current JSON benchmark file at each load; external publisher updates currently require source verification and a JSON update. The calculator does not automatically scrape brokerage websites. Overnight supervision requirements vary by child care license type; the model assumes no extra overnight payroll only if appropriate paid coverage is already separately included.

**Testing completed:** Syntax, arithmetic, scenario switching, director salary separation, 58-county options, offline rent fallback, and guided control logic were programmatically checked. A real mobile/browser, screen-reader, live Formspree, and user usability test remain necessary before deployment.

**Independent review prompt:** [docs/GEMINI_REVIEW_v10.6.0.txt](docs/GEMINI_REVIEW_v10.6.0.txt)

# Care with a Compass — The Director’s Desk · v10.4.0

**Live program:** https://rstenlund1.github.io/care-with-a-compass/?v=10.4.0

**v10.4.0 simulation and usability correction:** Independent static review found that the three expanded Director's Desk cases used repeated feedback, some harmful staffing decisions did not update live counts, and transportation cases inherited irrelevant medical-escort questions. This release adds individualized reasoning across all 36 original-Desk decision sets, connects leave/admission choices to live staffing or attendance, adds scenario-specific transportation questions for the remaining 22 transport steps, and removes a generic distractor-changing function that could overwrite safety effects. It places the primary decision before optional reference and staffing tools, collapses those tools, and puts coverage alerts with the focused decision. Eight foundational questions and selected branching alternatives now use more credible near-misses. The workplace transfer plan has a live character counter.

**Validation:** Syntax checks and programmatic scenario/variant generation checks passed. This is still an academic prototype; browser-based mobile and assistive-technology tests, child-care regulatory and clinical specialist validation, live Formspree delivery testing, and a learner pilot remain outstanding. This release does not establish certification validity.

# Care with a Compass — The Director's Desk · v10.2.0

**Live program:** https://rstenlund1.github.io/care-with-a-compass/

**Assessment-quality revision (v10.2.0):** The unified Consequence Lab draws three cases per session from eleven scenarios, including the three original Director's Desk stories reconstructed as 12-decision cases. Both answer order and case sequence vary automatically; randomization is not described to the learner. Case questions and choices were programmatically audited across 564 scenario/variant combinations. This release replaces repeated template distractors in the three expanded stories, adds realistic near-miss choices, removes arbitrary answer-length padding, and rewrites one weak distractor in applicable core decision sets. All choices retain decision-specific grading and explanatory feedback. Head Start-inspired topics remain attributed, separately from California child care licensing guidance.

**Validation:** All 564 scenario/variant combinations generated answer sets in a programmatic audit with no exceptions, and the updated script passed a syntax check. This is not a substitute for independent specialist review or a complete live-browser, accessibility, or learner pilot. Existing historical release documentation follows.

---

**v10.0.1 instructional enhancement:** The five existing foundation lessons now include extra director-level reasoning sections on safeguarding, reporting, staffing, emergencies and verifying transfer. All 72 applied questions retain individualized feedback; a correct response additionally displays the chosen option's explanation. The 36 connected follow-ups now show the original governing principle, why a selected path succeeds or needs correction, and a transfer question. The original Consequence Lab included eight case-specific prebrief lessons and a twelve-part decision-coaching framework. After every choice, the lab explains the relevant duty, compares a plausible alternative, and separates process quality from fictional outcome.

**Validation status:** Changes were reviewed against the source and the original backup was preserved. These new changes have NOT yet received a complete browser-based regression test, real learner pilot, independent clinical/legal content review, or validation of instructor email reports. The external GitHub Pages deployment cannot be confirmed merely by the existence of a repository commit; confirm the published page and inspect cached assets before presenting. Do not describe the educational simulations as validated professional certification or legally authoritative protocols.

**Preserved baseline:** backup/v9.9.1-before-consequence-lab-20261120

# Care with a Compass — The Director's Desk · v9.9.1

An interactive, consequential leadership-development **academic prototype** created for EDACE 830 at Kansas State University.

**Try the program:** https://rstenlund1.github.io/care-with-a-compass/?v=9.9.1

## What this release includes

- Five guided foundation chapters using 72 applied questions, 36 follow-ups, and the original chapter capstone.
- Three long-form applied case simulations, plus a staffing-resilience lab and evidence journal.
- A **five-stage adaptive final capstone**. The preceding decision changes the facts and available responses in the next stage, including twelve modeled conditional scenarios across stages two through five. Learners may review their decision trail and revise prior selections before submitting the local demonstration.
- A structured diagnostic assessment and a proposed, human-scored 30-day workplace transfer plan.
- A single guided Continue Training flow, open sidebar navigation, and clear Home / Start Over controls.

## Staffing budget clarification (v9.9.1)

The staffing lab separates **base teacher labor**, **additional teacher coverage**, and **total modeled teacher labor**. It assumes eight paid hours per scheduled teacher per day, plus 0/3/6/9 extra paid hours for no extra teacher, a 3-hour busy-period teacher, a 6-hour backup teacher, or both. Dollar totals respond to the number of teachers, reserve plan, and fully loaded hourly cost; the wage slider updates totals while being moved. These are instructional cost projections, not actual operating budgets. Additional cost is correctly $0 when no extra teacher is scheduled, but baseline labor still costs money. The 3-hour teacher is counted only during their extra shift; this classroom model assumes the 6-hour backup teacher is on shift during the selected incident.

## Responsive embedded learning chapters (v9.9.1)

The five-chapter iframe now reports its intrinsic content height rather than the full iframe viewport height. The outer page resizes the frame up or down with a small fixed margin, avoiding the accumulating blank white area between lesson screens. The measurement uses element bounds and a resize observer, including updates after images load. No lesson or question content was changed.

## Learner enrollment, reports, and completion certificate (v9.9.1)

- **Learner full name is required** on the main opening page beneath the introductory program description; there is no separate registration splash screen. Company, center, or organization is optional; participants acknowledge that their scores and progress may be shared with the program instructor. The instructor's identity appears on the program landing page.
- When learners complete each of the five foundational chapters, the embedded chapter engine supplies the **first-attempt and final response summary**, question/objective IDs, remedial attempts and live-coaching flag. The parent program also queues the final competency-assessment results and facilitator-review updates.
- Reports are stored locally pending email delivery. Their browser-side destination is in `index.html`: `window.CWC_REPORT_ENDPOINT=""`. **Email is NOT operational until the instructor configures a verified Formspree endpoint.** Never enter Outlook passwords or private service API keys into public site code. After a successful provider response, the local report is marked as sent. This is a demonstration, not a guaranteed tamperproof academic records system.
- A **printable completion certificate** is available after the five foundation chapters and original capstone, all three applied simulations, the staffing and evidence labs, and final competency assessment submission. It recognizes completion **regardless of the separate proposed 90/100 mastery gates**. The existing foundation-only certificate implementation remains in the independent chapter engine, but the integrated program uses the full-program completion check.
- A **Switch Learner** control clears local progress and identity on shared devices. Start Over preserves the enrolled learner's identity but clears program progress, reports and completion date for a new attempt.

For current enrollment and email setup details, see [REPORTING_SETUP.md](REPORTING_SETUP.md).

## Instructor reports with answer-level evidence (v9.9.1)

Chapter reporting now includes the **full wording of every initially missed question**, the learner's first response, the preferred response, the reasoning/feedback, the final response after practice, and a concise outcome line for every question. This is critical for instructors who prepare live coaching based on first-attempt gaps. Chapter reports are submitted explicitly; report submissions have unique learner-session IDs. Earlier-format pending chapter reports are archived locally without automatic replay, limiting duplicate emails. Successful service responses mark reports sent; ambiguous network failures disclose that delivery may already have occurred, and provide the actual validation error when available.

## Chapter submission and case variation (v9.9.1)

Each foundational chapter now ends with a **Review and Submit Chapter** checkpoint, displaying initial and final preferred-response counts. A deliberate **Submit Chapter Results to Instructor** button sends the learner's report to the configured Formspree service and displays success only after the service responds successfully. An independent **Continue to Next Chapter (testing)** button remains available during testing. Older completed chapters are preserved, with a reminder to submit any that do not yet have a successful local delivery record.

The surrounding chapter count updates from secure same-origin messages from the embedded lesson engine; it no longer remains stuck at 0/5 when a learner completes Chapter 1. Reporting events use distinct `chapter-submit-request` and `chapter-submit-status` messages so a chapter is not emailed merely by navigating onward.

The seven applied-case starting conditions now select **25 scenario adjustments** across the three long-form simulations. The variant changes actual question wording, situation details, and relevant response wording while preserving consistent scoring and essential safety duties.

Seven editorial photo banners reuse pictures already included in `images/` across applied cases, the staffing simulation, the evidence journal, the competency assessment and facilitator review.

## Final glossary polish (v9.9.1)

The legacy green/teal glossary popovers used in the embedded five-chapter curriculum now match the deep-purple instructor-guide definitions throughout the unified platform. The override is restricted to glossary buttons, hint symbols and open definition panels; assessment feedback colors and learning/scoring behavior are unchanged. Keyboard focus, Escape-to-close, and mobile positioning remain in the existing chapter engine.

## Final academic demonstration release (v9.9.1)

The completed prototype is prepared for an instructor-facing presentation. The five-stage final assessment has 243 decision sequences with consistent 70-point capstone weights and separate critical-safety gates. The five foundational chapters preserve first-attempt learner answer history, and chapter reports include the missed question, original selection, preferred choice, and subsequent improvement. Browser-side reports and progress are not tamperproof or authenticated.

The final facilitator rubric now requires an explicit **Enable facilitator scoring simulation** action. This is a teaching demonstration, NOT a secure reviewer login or independent verification. Any resulting score is provisional simulated performance, not an accredited award. The personalized completion certificate acknowledges completion of activities, not proof of mastery or professional qualification.

This release does not claim validated learning outcomes, a formally approved credential, or legally approved curriculum.

## Pilot scoring model

| Part | Points | Description |
|---|---:|---|
| Diagnostic classification and structural analysis | 20 | Five vignettes with two separate judgments each |
| Five-stage adaptive capstone | 70 | Safety 25, emergency handoff/coverage 15, reporting 10, evidence 10, downstream consequences 10 |
| Facilitator-reviewed workplace plan | 10 | Human scoring is demonstrated locally |
| **Total** | **100** | |

Proposed pilot competency gates: at least 90/100, at least four of five correct on each diagnostic objective, and **no designated critical safety failures**. A high numerical score cannot override a missed safety gate.

The scoring threshold is a program design choice, not a California regulatory or validated certification standard.

## Development and evidence

- `index.html` loads the modular application, data, lesson, and citation assets.
- `js/v92-app.js` contains navigation, stage selection, branch-sensitive scoring, and browser-local output.
- `js/v92-data.js` contains the case and assessment data, including conditional assessment scenarios.
- `js/v94-lessons.js` supplies guided instruction and vocabulary.
- `js/v96-references.js` supplies supporting legal, regulatory, and adult-learning references.
- `css/v92.css` includes responsive layouts.

The current release was compilation-checked and programmatically exercised on all **243** possible five-stage option sequences, with 12 distinct decision-dependent follow-up conditions and zero automated assessment-rendering errors.

## Limitations and pre-pilot work

This is a **working demonstration, not an accredited course, verified credentialing platform, or evidence of measured learning outcomes**. Its local browser storage cannot verify participants or independent facilitators; there is no cloud synchronization or multi-learner dashboard. The current practice assessment allows pre-submission revision and is not a secure first-attempt examination.

Before a real pilot, the program requires independent California regulatory and child-protection review, live usability/accessibility testing, authenticated facilitator scoring, controlled assessment administration, and genuinely equivalent reassessment forms. Source citations illustrate decision frameworks; the prototype is not legal advice or a replacement for current law.

All instructional case material is fictionalized and deidentified. The project does not claim approval, funding, partnership, or endorsement from Kansas State University, Pathways LA, or California credentialing agencies.

## Protected historical baseline

The previous release is preserved on branch `backup/v9.6.1-before-branching-capstone-20261113`.

# Care with a Compass · Instructor Email Reporting Setup (v10.6.0)

The public site runs on GitHub Pages, so it cannot send an email itself. For a short supervised pilot, use a verified **Formspree form** to send instructor notifications to **rickstenlund@outlook.com**.

## Connect a Formspree form

1. Create and verify a Formspree account at https://formspree.io/ using the instructor's Outlook email.
2. Choose **New Form**. Name it **Care with a Compass – Training Reports** and set the recipient/target email to **rickstenlund@outlook.com**.
3. Under **Workflow → Validation**, check whether a default *required email* rule is enabled. Remove that rule if present: the training deliberately requires only the learner's **name**, with an **optional organization**, and does not request a learner email address.
4. Under **Project Settings → Restrict to Domain**, enter `rstenlund1.github.io` (without `https://` or a path). This reduces casual unauthorized submissions, but it is not authentication.
5. Under **Integration**, copy the **public form endpoint**, in the format `https://formspree.io/f/xxxxxxxx`. Do **not** copy API keys, email passwords, or a private dashboard link.
6. Edit the public GitHub repository `index.html`. Locate `window.CWC_REPORT_ENDPOINT=""` and change the empty quotes to your **exact Formspree endpoint**. Do not alter the surrounding script.
7. Confirm that the published site loads the updated `index.html`. Test registration in the main introductory panel and one explicit Submit Chapter Results action with an imaginary adult's name; verify that **Formspree shows a submission and the instructor Outlook inbox receives the notification**. Check Junk/Spam as needed.
8. Test final assessment submission and optional facilitator scoring. Repeat with an incomplete answer path to confirm coaching gaps are listed correctly.

## Expected volume

Each participant can generate **five learner-submitted chapter notices**, **one final-assessment notice**, and **one instructor-review notice**: approximately **seven submissions per participant**. Fifteen learners can therefore generate roughly **105 notices**. Formspree's published free plan currently includes **50 monthly submissions**; a paid plan is likely needed for the full proposed pilot. Pricing and terms may change; see https://formspree.io/plans/.

## What goes into the reports

Every report contains the learner's self-entered name, optional organization, browser-local session ID, date, and event type. Chapter emails now include a separate first_attempt_mistakes field containing each initially missed question's full scenario, original selected answer, preferred answer, feedback/rationale, and final remediation result, plus an all_question_outcomes field listing all question IDs, objectives, attempts and first/final selections. The instructor can therefore prepare coaching without looking up question IDs. The final assessment adds scored portions, gate metrics, and selected **option IDs**, while facilitator updates provide the manual score and provisional outcome.

**Raw open-ended learner reflections, details about children, family names, and staff case narratives are deliberately excluded.** The enrollment screen tells learners that their performance will be sent to the instructor and warns against entering other people's private information.

## Reliability and limitations

- A browser may fail to receive a response even when Formspree accepted the report. Before retrying an ambiguous send, check the Formspree submissions dashboard and report_id to avoid duplicate messages.\n- No report goes to a provider while `window.CWC_REPORT_ENDPOINT` is empty.
- Reports are queued **in the learner's browser** and delivered on completion or a later visit once the endpoint is configured. Failed submissions remain locally queued for a later retry. Clearing browser storage, switching learner, or starting over may discard undelivered records.
- The site does not provide secure logins, attendance verification, confirmed facilitator identity, tamperproof scores, or a central class roster.
- The completion certificate documents finished activities and is separate from the proposed **90/100 plus safety-gates** competency assessment.
- For formal credentialing or legally regulated educational records, move reporting to a protected server with authenticated users, stronger consent/access controls, and encrypted records. Formspree is suitable only if the program's consent, privacy, and institutional requirements allow sending these fields through this provider.

## References

- Formspree form creation: https://help.formspree.io/articles/building-your-form/building-an-html-form
- Formspree AJAX submissions: https://help.formspree.io/articles/building-your-form/submit-forms-with-javascript-ajax
- Formspree Workflow validation: https://help.formspree.io/articles/building-your-form/getting-started-with-workflow
- Domain restriction: https://help.formspree.io/articles/form-and-project-settings/restrict-to-domain
- Plans: https://formspree.io/plans/

All embedded program photographs are supplied by the project owner and should not be reused without authorization. Training content and third-party references remain subject to their respective rights.

# Care with a Compass v7.2 — consequence-driven branching design

The two source files for branch data are `data/branching.json` (authoritative, human-readable) and `js/branching.js` (browser-readable, generated from the JSON by `tools/build_branching_js.py`). Branch data loads before `js/app.js` and is embedded in the fully offline single-file build.

## Branch behavior

**Chapter decision labs:** For every Chapter 1–5 lab, each of its **four initial decisions** leads to a different second-stage scenario, question, four answer choices, and feedback. There are **20 distinct follow-up situations**, including consequences of the preferred decision. A first decision can be changed while exploring the lab; its second-stage selection resets correctly.

**Four-stage capstone:** The opening emergency question has four options. At stages 2, 3, and 4, the learner receives one of **four complete, different scenarios and option sets** based on the exact prior choice, for **12 distinct later-stage scenes**. Responses are scored from the actual selected branch options rather than a separate matrix. The retrospective reconstructs the actual sequence and individual feedback for the route the learner took. This is a branching DAG, not an open-ended generative simulation; paths can converge by design.

## Instructional challenge

The successful Stage 3 mandated-reporting path deliberately leads to an **unverified counter-allegation** in Stage 4. This does not imply retaliation always occurs, and it does not undermine the original reporting obligation. Learners must document, cooperate with licensing, protect confidentiality, maintain interim child safeguards, and support staff who report in good faith.

## Invariants

- The 72-question bank, original chapter lessons, course citations, scoring schema, images, and question editor are unchanged from v7.1.
- The application stores progress under a new v7.2 storage key, so incomplete v7.1 capstone selections cannot be interpreted against new branch choices.
- Every branch has four graded options with exactly one `2` (strongest), one `1` (defensible with conditions), and two `0` (review). No unsafe choice receives partial credit.
- The script is offline and does not use AI inference or network requests.
- A certificate records completion of guided practice, *not* an independent competence credential.

## Editing

Update `data/branching.json`, run `python tools/build_branching_js.py` and `python tools/build_standalone.py`, then `python tools/qa_release.py`. Branches are stored outside the question editor: that editor still manages only the 72 question-bank items, not branch scenarios.

# GEMINI INDEPENDENT ADVERSARIAL REVIEW — CARE WITH A COMPASS v10.7.0
Date: November 21, 2026
Live: https://rstenlund1.github.io/care-with-a-compass/?v=10.7.0
Source: https://github.com/Rstenlund1/care-with-a-compass
Budget logic: js/budget-planner.js
County rent data: data/california-budget-benchmarks.json
Training shell and progress: js/v92-app.js
Primary styling: css/v92.css
Consequence simulation: consequence-lab.html

You are reviewing an academic child care leadership training prototype and proposed financial-planning tool. Be skeptical, specific, and evidence-based. Do not praise or predict a perfect grade. A prior review of v10.5.0 is not evidence that v10.7.0 is correct. Quote exact question text/code and identify file names, steps, and reproduced outcomes.

PRIORITY 1 — NAVIGATION AND ONBOARDING
Walk the site as a first-time learner. Can a person immediately understand how to enroll, start, continue, explore modules, see remaining work, and resume? Does the overall training progress bar accurately count the six chapters, chapter capstone, three consequence cases, staffing exercise, tuition planner, evidence journal, and assessment? Does progress persist after refresh, switching tabs, using a separate case window, and returning later? Does changing budget data erroneously count as completing staffing? Are Continue buttons visible, enabled appropriately, and focused correctly? Find dead ends, confusing wording, duplicated menus, inaccessible controls, unwanted scroll jumps, and extraneous text.

PRIORITY 2 — REAL VISUAL AND MOBILE REVIEW
If browser access is available, inspect desktop, 768px tablet, 390px phone, and 320px phone. Examine layout hierarchy, typography, contrast, whitespace, scrolling, navigation, mobile form input sizes, form focus, slider precision, source labels, data-heavy cards, error states, and the prominence of the actual decision question. Test keyboard-only and screen reader announcements if possible. If no browser is available, identify findings as code-derived hypotheses and request screenshots; do not claim live visual verification.

PRIORITY 3 — BUDGET AND TUITION MATHEMATICS
Test js/budget-planner.js from the source, not simply by reading the displayed sample totals:
- Verify tuition and respite revenue, part-time attendance, overnight-only children, overnight nights/stays, and supplies.
- Verify teacher FTE wages, aide FTE wages, payroll load, extra overnight hours, and DIRECTOR SALARY as three clearly separate concepts.
- The director's desired salary is an operating expense, not teacher/aide payroll and NOT the target business profit. Raising it $1,000 must lower monthly surplus $1,000 and raise required tuition appropriately.
- Desired operating profit is after director pay. Verify zero-enrollment and extreme-input handling, currency and negative values, real-vs-example scenario isolation, and effect of resetting examples.
- Test county rent selection for all 58 California counties. Verify published region rate versus statewide fallback, unit conversions for annual/monthly retail asking rents, source labels, data period, and override via actual monthly rent or square-foot footage slider and custom rate.
- Source records are published-market PROXIES, not a true child care property or official statewide average. The fallback is an unweighted average of eight regional benchmarks and must be recomputed if regional figures change. The site fetches the repository's dated JSON when loaded; this is not proof that it automatically crawls market publishers.
- Test NNN/CAM, insurance, utilities percentage of rent, food, incidentals and director compensation separately. Identify omissions like taxes, debt service, vacancies and payroll scheduling.
- Independently calculate monthly break-even enrollment, tuition needed for the profit target, and capacity infeasibility. Challenge every fixed-cost assumption as enrollment increases.
- Test a 24/7 operator scenario with children who attend only overnight. Do not equate sleeping children with automatically permitted sleeping supervision. Check family child care home vs child care center law and whether paid qualified overnight staffing is actually budgeted.
- Evaluate whether the financial outputs are understandable to a director who has never studied accounting.

PRIORITY 4 — SCORING AND BRANCHING
Run all 11 case families, all variants and all 12 decisions. Do not accept mere syntax or 2,256 structural checks as proof of ethical validity. Check realistic distractors, near misses, consequences actually updating state, appropriate factual and regulatory citations, stale incorrect questions, and whether outcomes reflect recovery after a mistake. Recalculate answer-length bias, identifying worst offending questions.

PRIORITY 5 — EXHAUSTIVE WRITING, DESCRIPTIONS AND STORY CONTINUITY
Audit every learner-facing string, not just sample questions. Check headings, descriptions, chapter lessons, glossary, 72 main questions, 36 follow-up prompts, branching answer alternatives, all 11 scenario families, 12 stages and variants, recovery feedback, staffing exercises, budget fields, rent-source labels, instructions, navigation, progress messaging, completion/debrief text, and final assessment. Look for awkward or unnatural sentences, spelling, grammar, redundant wording, unclear jargon, inexplicable numbering, inconsistent terms and overlong descriptions.
Treat misleading descriptions and narrative contradictions as functional defects: answer choices not matching a question, an ambulance in a non-medical transport case, an unauthorized adult being described as authorized, a staff member leaving without changing coverage, shifting timelines, different names/pronouns, unsupported facts, feedback describing an action the learner did not choose, or previously resolved problems still being described as active.
For the finance and licensing screens, verify clarity of enrolled versus present children; monthly versus annual and per-square-foot units; wages versus director salary versus business profit; actual rent versus a regional market proxy or constructed statewide fallback; software loading an updated JSON file versus automatically finding new publisher rates; overnight sleeping versus required qualified supervision; and needed tuition versus a locally affordable/competitive price.
Give an exact location, verbatim current text, reason it is wrong or confusing, and a revised sentence/button/option for EACH confirmed issue. Sort true factual/narrative errors ahead of subjective style changes. Keep the author's voice and examples rather than making prose generically formal. Explicitly identify uninspected paths. Assess if an inexperienced director can understand each direction without an explanation from the developer.

PRIORITY 6 — APA, ACADEMIC CONSISTENCY AND PRESENTATION
Compare the short submission paper, portfolio paper, slideshow and speaker notes with v10.7.0 if supplied. Treat old version statements as needing revision, not proof the current site is wrong. Check page limits, scope and references. Evaluate whether the budget and overall progress claims have been adequately incorporated into academic descriptions. Avoid inventing performed pilot studies or learner outcomes.

REPORT FORMAT

# Care with a Compass v7.2 — Test and release notes

**Release:** 2026-11-10. Baseline: audited v7.1. Tests were run on the newly generated v7.2 files, not inferred from v7.1.

## Automated source validation

- 72 assessed questions across five chapters: 12/14/18/14/14; 8 select-all questions.
- Original question keys and qualitative feedback are unchanged from v7.1. Python schema tests confirm unique IDs, answer/feedback parity, valid sources, forbidden retired subsidy language absent, and editable data parity.
- `data/branching.json` contains 20 distinct lab branches and 12 distinct later-stage capstone branches. Every one of the 32 paths has distinct context and graded choices. Every scene has 4 answers graded 0, 0, 1, 2. The new runtime grades from the selected scene's embedded option score, avoiding a separate grading matrix.
- JavaScript syntax passed for the app, question data, and new branching data.
- Standalone HTML contains all 14 inline WebP photographs, all scripts and CSS, and no external application dependencies.

## Actual Chromium browser exercise

Ran Chromium using an inline copy of the generated standalone HTML, since the managed test environment blocks local `file://` navigation (`net::ERR_BLOCKED_BY_ADMINISTRATOR`). This test **does not prove that the modular folder version loaded over `file://`**, though file names and syntax are checked separately.

- For every chapter lab, the four distinct initial choices revealed four **different** follow-up situations and sets of options; stage-two answer click produced feedback.
- For the capstone at stages 2–4, each of four incoming prior-choice states revealed a different scenario, choices, and clickable graded feedback.
- Exhaustively evaluated all **256 possible four-choice capstone decision sequences**, ensuring each selected branch offers four choices, grades to 0/1/2, and generates four retrospective cards.
- Completed the full best-choice capstone route (step 1 C, then 2 A, then 3 A, then 4 A). The correct mandated report leads to an unexpected unverified complaint, and the completed retrospective reflects all four actual scenes.
- Verified 72 original items still yield score 2 for their correct key. Eight select-all items were preserved.
- Mobile 390×844 viewport displayed without horizontal page overflow, and no uncaught JavaScript page errors were logged in the test sessions.
- Tested switching a chapter lab's first decision after selecting a follow-up: the previous follow-up selection correctly resets.

## Limitations / remaining human review

- A professional should still review all newly drafted branching narratives and current California reporting/licensing law before offering the academy as authoritative staff training. Automated tests cannot certify legal correctness or pedagogical validity.
- Native OS print dialogs, assistive technology on actual user devices, and all combinations of browser versions were not tested. Certificate printing behavior retains the v7.1 implementation.
- Branches are **authored decision trees**. The next situation depends on the previous selected choice, and different choices can eventually converge. The course does not invent novel scenes using an AI model, does not continuously simulate time, and does not model all possible real-world consequences.

# Source verification notes — release candidate

## Pathways LA subsidy co-payments
The user's reported newer process is that Pathways LA collects parent co-payments and passes funds through to providers. As of the review on 2026-11-10, the agency’s publicly accessible provider-payments and parent FAQ pages still state that co-payments (the difference above the Regional Market Rate ceiling) are paid directly to the provider, while **family fees** are a distinct category. This claim has **not** been incorporated as a course fact pending current written confirmation from Pathways LA.

Official sources: https://pathwaysla.org/for-providers/provider-payments/ and https://pathwaysla.org/for-parents/faq-forms/

## Infant ratio correction
22 CCR § 101416.5(b)(1) permits qualified aides as substitutions only with a fully qualified teacher supervising no more than 12 infants AND each aide directly supervising no more than four infants. The review's claim that one teacher plus one aide may cover 12 infants is incorrect. Subsection (c) concerns directors counting in ratio; subsection (d) has a separate sleeping-infant provision.
Source: https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/california/22-CCR-101416.5

## Scope
This release incorporates a technical and content audit but is not a legal opinion. The source map is provided for additional verification of fact-specific reporting duties.

## v7.1 Gemini reconciliation
The retired 50% reimbursement paragraph was removed from Chapter 3, the unpublished exceptional-needs URL removed, and academic references in the Sources drawer are non-clickable. C1Q11 is again a genuine multiple-select item, and capstone score levels are embedded in each exact response. Branch consequences now vary with the previous decision. The complete release is verified with `tools/qa_release.py`.

"""Bundle HTML/CSS/JS/WebP into a truly standalone offline HTML file."""
from pathlib import Path
import base64,re
root=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
html=(root/'index.html').read_text(encoding='utf-8')
css=(root/'css/styles.css').read_text(encoding='utf-8')
html=html.replace('<link rel="stylesheet" href="css/styles.css">','<style>\n'+css+'\n</style>')
for src in ('js/data.js','js/branching.js','js/app.js'):
 js=(root/src).read_text(encoding='utf-8')
 if src.endswith('/app.js'):
  for image in (root/'images').glob('*.webp'):
   image_path='images/'+image.name
   image_uri='data:image/webp;base64,'+base64.b64encode(image.read_bytes()).decode('ascii')
   assert f'"{image_path}"' in js,image_path
   js=js.replace(f'"{image_path}"',f'"{image_uri}"')
 js=js.replace('</script',r'<\/script')
 tag=f'<script src="{src}"></script>'
 assert tag in html,src
 html=html.replace(tag,'<script>\n'+js+'\n</script>')
assert '<script src=' not in html
assert html.count('data:image/webp;base64,')==14
(root/'Care_with_a_Compass_Standalone_Offline.html').write_text(html,encoding='utf-8')
